evidence.section_title: Program of intensive interpersonal psychotherapy for depressed adolescents with suicidal risk
evidence.quote: [/page/2/Text/10] The IPT-A-IN shared the same principles with the IPT-A, which collected target symptoms related to the current interpersonal problem domains, including interpersonal conflict, interpersonal sensitivity, role transition, and grief. In IPT-A-IN, which, following IPT-A, adopts biopsychosocial viewpoints...
[/page/3/Text/6] The students in the IPT-A-IN and TAU intervention groups were assessed on the BDI, BSS, BAI and BHS before and after intervention during the same 6-week period.
[/page/3/Text/10] students in the IPT-A-IN and TAU groups
[/page/4/Text/7] IPT-A-IN, intensive interpersonal psychotherapy for depressed adolescents with suicidal risk

The present results show that school-based IPT-A-IN has superior effects, compared to TAU, on reducing severity of depression, suicidal ideation, anxiety, and hopelessness in depressed adolescents with suicide risk in schools.

The present study demonstrated that school-based IPT-A-IN is effective in reducing severity of depression, suicidal ideation, anxiety and hopelessness in depressed adolescents with suicide risk in a twosession intensive intervention each week for 6 weeks.
A total of 35 students (12 boys, 23 girls ... assigned to the IPT-A-IN arm, and 38 students (13 boys, 25 girls ... assigned to the TAU arm.

A senior psychiatrist used the Chinese version of the Structured Clinical Interview (SCID-I)26,27 to determine the axis I psychiatric diagnoses on the DSM-IV-TR28 for the selected students. ... a total of 73 depressed students with suicidal risk were recruited into the intervention program

We also found that most of the present participants were not depressed enough to be diagnosed with major depressive disorder. Interpersonal conflicts with family members and peers, however, were very prevalent among the present participants, which was also found by Fordwood et al.38 Facing these interpersonal conflicts, the adolescents developed significant symptoms, and most of them had comorbid anxiety or insomnia. Two subjects (one from each group) were advised to go to hospital for medication combined with psychological intervention. As for the other subjects with depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation, whom the psychiatrist judged did not need to receive treatment in clinic or be admitted to hospital, the school counselors suggested that they receive IPT, either in hospitals or in schools.

evidence.quote: [page/0/Text/7] A total of 347 students from one-fifth of the classes of a high school in southern Taiwan completed the Beck Depression Inventory-II, the Beck Scale for Suicide Ideation, the Beck Anxiety Inventory and the Beck Hopelessness Scale for screening for suicidal risk.

Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II), the Beck Scale for Suicide Ideation (BSS), the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), and the Beck Hopelessness Scale (BHS) ... A senior psychiatrist used the Chinese version of the Structured Clinical Interview (SCID-I) ... The psychiatrist also evaluated the students' severity of depression and suicidal risk.
[/page/3/Text/6] Assessment tools were self-report scales, therefore, evaluators would remind students who had omissions in the questionnaire and help to calculate the total scores.
